newsitem.title: USA: CHRISTOPHER HINTS CZECHS WILL JOIN NATO SOON.
newsitem.headline: CHRISTOPHER HINTS CZECHS WILL JOIN NATO SOON.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher gave a broad hint on Monday that the Czech Republic would be among the first wave of former Warsaw Pact countries admitted to NATO.

A summmit next spring or early summer of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation will name the first group of East European states to be accepted into the Western alliance, which currently has 16 members.

"The Czech Republic is certainly taking all the right steps to prepare for possible NATO membership," Christopher said before talks with Czech Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus. "Just as important as that, their armed forces are gaining experience in serving together with ours and other NATO members in Bosnia."
Czech forces had also made a "vital contribution" in Eastern Slavonia, a part of Croatia due to be handed over to the Zagreb government by Serb forces, he said.

Western officials said key requirements for countries aspiring to join NATO were keeping armed forces under civilian control, readiness to assume the financial obligations, and inter-operability with NATO forces.
Diplomats said the leading contenders for the first wave of new members were the Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary and possibly the former Yugoslav republic of Slovenia.

Klaus said: "We have the feeling that we belong to NATO. Just the 50 years of communism prevented us from being one of the founding fathers of NATO ... so we hope that the moment of our entry is approaching."
The Czech premier said he did not believe the decision on whether to admit former Soviet allies should depend on the views of Russia, which expressed strong opposition.
"I don't think it's necessary to combine those two things together. I think that they will be sort of independent," he told reporters. REUTER 302230 GMT sep 96
